meta.name: Collect packaging declarations from CSV with forms, AI agents and email

name: PPWR Data Screener: collects packaging declarations from vendors, validates and follows up.

parameters.content:
## PPWR Data Screener: collects packaging declarations from vendors, validates and follows up.

### Who's it for

Anyone who has to get a declaration of conformity out of every packaging supplier and check each one.

### How it works

**Send.** Upload a CSV of suppliers and items. Every row gets an email with a link to the form.

**Screen.** The supplier fills the form and attaches their declaration. An agent reads the document and a checklist in one Code node decides. **No model produces a pass or a fail.**

**Answer.** Complete, and they get a confirmation. Not complete, and they get a named list of what is missing plus the form link again.

### How to set up

Drag your chat model onto the two agent nodes and add an SMTP credential to the two email nodes. Open **Configuration** and paste the form URL from **Supplier declaration form**.

### Requirements

A chat model of your choice, an SMTP credential, and n8n 1.7 or newer for the agent node.

---

**This checks declarations for completeness and consistency. It is not a conformity assessment and it is not legal advice.** The checklist here is an example. Read it and change it before you point it at real suppliers.

**It keeps no record and the form link is not private.**

### Send

Upload a CSV, everybody on it gets a link.

Columns: `supplier_name`, `contact_email`, `internal_sku`, and `description` if you have it. A row that cannot be used is reported by line number and the rest still go out.

### Start

Two ways in. You upload a CSV of suppliers, or a supplier submits their declaration. Both land on **Configuration**, which every later node reads.

One supplier, one item, one attachment. The form is the only thing they ever see.

### Read

The agent reports what the document says. It does not decide whether anything passes.

**Drag your own chat model onto it.** Any of them works, and swapping it cannot change a verdict.

### Decide

One Code node holds the checklist. Same submission, same answer, every time.

### Answer

Complete, and they get a confirmation.

Not complete, and they get a named list plus the form link again, so a resubmission is one click and not an email thread.

nodes.name: Load your supplier list
nodes.notes:
This is the one you open. The supplier never sees it.

One email per row, so a supplier with forty items gets forty emails. Group them in Build the invitation if that matters to you.

parameters.formDescription:
Upload a CSV of the suppliers and items you need a declaration for. Everybody on it gets an email with a link to the form.

Columns: supplier_name, contact_email, internal_sku, description.

nodes.name: Find the list
nodes.notes: Form uploads land under a key that has moved between n8n versions. This takes whatever arrived.

nodes.name: CSV to rows
nodes.notes: One item per row, with the header names as keys. Capitalisation and spacing in the header do not matter; the next node normalises them.

nodes.name: Check the list
nodes.notes:
The whole file gets checked before anything is sent.

A row with no email, or the same reference twice for one supplier, is reported by line number and dropped. The rest still go out. A file where nothing is usable stops here with the reasons.

nodes.name: Build the invitation
nodes.notes:
One email per row, carrying the form link and their reference.

Runs once over every row, not once per row. A Code node set to run per item cannot call .first() on another node, and this one reads Configuration.

There is no token on the link. Anyone holding it can submit against any reference, which is fine for a handful of suppliers you already know.

nodes.name: Send the request
nodes.notes: Swap for Gmail, Outlook or anything else. The body arrives as plain text, already assembled.

nodes.name: What went out
nodes.notes: What you get back: how many went, and every row that did not, with its line number.

nodes.name: Supplier declaration form
nodes.notes:
Copy this node's form URL into Configuration. It goes in the invitation and again in the gap notice, so a resubmission is the same form.

Leave a field blank and the checklist reports it as missing. Nothing gets rejected on the way in.

parameters.formDescription:
Tell us about this packaging item and attach your declaration of conformity.

We check it for completeness and consistency. That is not a conformity assessment and it is not legal advice.

nodes.name: Configuration
nodes.notes:
Everything you need to change is in here.

form_url: paste the production URL from Supplier declaration form. Both emails use it.

declaration_max_age_days: how old a declaration you will still accept.

confidence_floor: how sure the agent has to be before a value it read gets used, instead of being reported as unconfirmed.

assignments.name: disclaimer
assignments.value: This message reports a completeness and consistency check only. It is not a conformity assessment and it is not legal advice.

nodes.name: Which form was it?
nodes.notes:
Both forms come through Configuration, so there is one place to set things, and this sends each one down its own lane.

It tells them apart by a field only the supplier form has. Rename 'Your company' on that form and you have to change it here too.

nodes.name: Find the attachment
nodes.notes: Same trick as the CSV lane: take whatever key the upload arrived under.

nodes.name: Declaration to text
nodes.notes: A scanned declaration has no text layer and comes back empty. The checklist reports it as a document it could not read, which is the truth.

nodes.name: Read the declaration
nodes.notes:
Drag your own chat model onto this node.

It reads and reports. Nothing it returns can produce a pass or a fail, so whichever model you use, the answer the supplier gets is the same.

parameters.text:
=Read this packaging declaration and report what it says.

--- document ---
{{ ($json.text || '').slice(0, 12000) }}
--- end ---

options.systemMessage:
You read one supplier packaging declaration and report what it says. You do not judge it.

Return only JSON, no prose and no markdown fences, in exactly this shape:

{
  "signatory": { "value": "", "confidence": 0 },
  "declaration_date": { "value": "", "confidence": 0 },
  "primary_material": { "value": "", "confidence": 0 },
  "pfas_statement": { "value": "", "confidence": 0 },
  "bpa_statement": { "value": "", "confidence": 0 }
}

Rules:

- value is the text as it appears in the document. Do not paraphrase and do not translate.
- confidence is 0 to 1. Use it honestly. 0.9 means you are reading it off the page, 0.4 means you are inferring it from context.
- A field the document does not mention gets an empty value and a confidence of 0. Never invent one, and never carry a value over from an example.
- declaration_date must be YYYY-MM-DD. If the document writes it another way, convert it. If the day and month are ambiguous, return an empty value.
- pfas_statement and bpa_statement are the sentence in which the document addresses that substance, whether it says the substance is present or absent. Silence is an empty value.
- primary_material is the packaging material, not the product inside it.

You are reading a document somebody signed. If it does not say something, say that it does not say it.

nodes.name: Parse what was read
nodes.notes:
Models wrap JSON in fences and put a sentence in front of it. This strips both.

An answer it cannot parse counts as nothing read. That is a finding, not a failed run.

nodes.name: Merge answers
nodes.notes:
What the supplier typed wins. The document only fills blanks, and only above the confidence floor.

A confident reading that contradicts what they typed gets flagged, never written over. The supplier is the one signing.

nodes.name: Run the checklist
nodes.notes:
This is where the pass or fail happens, and the only node that decides anything.

The rules are the list at the top: an id, a severity, the sentence the supplier reads, and a function returning pass, fail or skip. Add a rule by adding an entry to the list. You should never need another node.

Skip means the rule did not apply, and a skipped rule is not reported to anyone.

nodes.name: Everything present?
nodes.notes: An advisory finding does not stop an item. Only a blocker does.

nodes.name: Build the confirmation
nodes.notes: Fixed sentences and the checklist output. Nothing here is drafted.

nodes.name: Draft the covering paragraph
nodes.notes:
Drag your own chat model onto this node too.

It writes the two sentences above the list and nothing else. The list underneath is rendered by the checklist and is not up for editing here.

options.systemMessage:
You write one short paragraph to a supplier whose packaging declaration is missing something.

You will be shown the list of what is outstanding. That list is already written and will be printed under your paragraph exactly as it is. Your job is the sentence or two above it.

Rules:

- Two or three sentences. Plain English. No greeting and no sign-off; both are added around you.
- Never mention a check id. They appear in the list below you.
- Never add a point that is not in the list, and never say a point is resolved.
- Do not apologise, do not thank them twice, and do not say 'kindly'.
- Write to somebody who is busy and did not do anything wrong. Most gaps are a missing sentence in a template, not negligence.

Return the paragraph and nothing else.

nodes.name: Build the gap notice
nodes.notes:
Assembles the email, and puts the form link back in it so the supplier can resubmit without asking anyone for it.

If the drafted paragraph mentions a check that did not run, this stops the send. A supplier chasing a rule that never ran is worse than no covering note at all.

nodes.name: Send the answer
nodes.notes: Swap this for Gmail, Outlook, Slack or a webhook without touching anything before it. The body arrives as plain text, already assembled.

nodes.name: Show the supplier the result
nodes.notes: The supplier sees this straight away. The detail goes to them by email.

parameters.completionTitle: ={{ $('Run the checklist').first().json.complete ? 'Declaration received and complete' : 'Declaration received' }}
parameters.completionMessage: ={{ $('Run the checklist').first().json.complete ? 'Thank you. We have what we need for this item and have emailed you a confirmation.' : 'Thank you. Some points are still outstanding. We have emailed you the list and a link to send it again.' }}
